claims.claim: Health insurance is a contract that requires the insurer to pay some or all of the insured person's health care costs in exchange for a premium (HealthCare.gov's working definition; Investopedia describes the same contract).
The premium is the amount you pay for your health insurance every month, and it is separate from the costs you pay when you use care, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance.
The deductible is the amount you pay for covered health care services before your insurance plan starts to pay.
A copayment is a fixed amount you pay for a covered health care service after the deductible, usually at the time of the visit.
Coinsurance is the percentage of the costs of a covered health care service you pay after the deductible, such as 20%.

The out-of-pocket maximum is the most you have to pay for covered services in a plan year; after you spend that amount on deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for in-network care, the plan pays 100% of the costs of covered benefits.

A plan's network is the group of providers and facilities it has contracted with; in-network copayments are usually less than out-of-network copayments, and the out-of-pocket maximum applies to in-network care and services.

Coverage commonly comes through job-based health plans offered by employers or through Marketplace plans, which must cover 10 essential health benefits; open enrollment is the yearly period (November 1 - January 15 for Marketplace plans, with job-based plans on their own schedules) when people can enroll.
Most health plans must cover a set of preventive services, like screening tests and check-ups, at no cost to the member.

Honest framing: health insurance is protection against large, unpredictable medical bills; the premium is the predictable monthly cost, while deductibles, copays, and coinsurance are the shares paid when care is used, capped by the out-of-pocket maximum.

conflictingEvidence: Definition wording varies slightly across sources: HealthCare.gov defines health insurance as a contract that requires your health insurer to pay some or all of your health care costs in exchange for a premium, while Investopedia describes a contract in which a company agrees to pay all or some of the insured person's healthcare costs in return for payment of a monthly premium. The lesson uses the working definition 'a contract that pays for medical care in exchange for premiums' and attributes it to HealthCare.gov.

Plan details (deductible sizes, copay amounts, coinsurance percentages, network rules) vary by plan, employer, and state, and figures change yearly; the lesson states only the general mechanics and labels every number an illustrative example, not a guarantee.

Investopedia's live page is behind a bot check; its definition was verified through the June 2025 Wayback Machine snapshot of the same URL. CFPB's consumer-education pages on health insurance basics were retired (404 on 2026-08-21), so CFPB is not cited here.
